statements.quote: The bills we passed today are critical to addressing the security challenges with AI, providing Congress with oversight over the sale of advanced AI chips to our adversaries, and supercharging American AI leadership to beat China.
statements.context: Baird applauded House Foreign Affairs Committee passage of bills including the AI OVERWATCH Act (H.R. 6875), which he cosponsors, on AI chip sales to adversaries.
statements.reason: Names only general national security challenges and competition with China, with no catastrophic danger from AI itself (rulings 4 and 5).

statements.quote: Training in STEM is paramount in our increasingly digital security landscape, especially as our adversaries pursue advances in artificial intelligence, surveillance technology, and next-generation communications infrastructure,
statements.context: Baird introduced the Tech Diplomacy Training Act (H.R. 8212) requiring science and technology training for Foreign Service officers.
statements.reason: Mentions AI only as a field of competition with adversaries such as China, which is not catastrophic risk (ruling 5).

slowdown.note: No statement found on slowing frontier AI development.

pause.note: No statement found on pausing frontier AI development.

intl.note: No statement found on coordinating with China on the pace of AI; his AI remarks frame China as a rival to beat.

rsi.note: No statement found on banning self-improving AI.

record: Cosponsor of the AI OVERWATCH Act (H.R. 6875), on congressional oversight of advanced AI chip sales to adversaries such as China; this is export control, not catastrophic-risk policy.
grade_reason: In 2026 Baird spoke about AI only as a national security and competition-with-China issue; no statement acknowledging catastrophic risk from AI was found.
